text: Aurillac – Le Lioran: 166.6km / 3800m+ Two years ago at the Tour de France, Jonas Vingegaard pulled off an improbable sprint win against Tadej Pogačar. Vingegaard profited after his rival put in a big attack on the first category Puy Mary Pas de Peyrol but then appeared to get the hunger knock. Pogačar weakened dramatically and was caught by Vingegaard on the cat. 1 Col de Pertus, then was edged out in a tight sprint. Both of those climbs return this year, being preceded by a trio of cat. 3 ascents plus the second category Col de la Griffoul. It’s a very draining day in the saddle and even if the last of the day’s seven climbs is just a category 3, the accumulated fatigue will put riders under real pressure prior to a very short drop down to the finish line.
